name: Sheber
overview: Sheber was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) and Maacah. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or narrative details recorded beyond his genealogy. This places him within the important lineage of Judah, contributing to the broader biblical record of the tribe's descendants.
namesAndTitles: The name Sheber may mean 'lion' or possibly refer to 'breaking' or 'crushing' grain, reflecting Hebrew roots. These meanings suggest strength or a process of breaking, though the Scripture does not indicate that the name was given by God or carries a special title.
familyAndRelationships: Sheber is recorded as the son of Chelubai, also known as Caleb, and Maacah. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these parental relationships, situating him within a known Judean family line.
scriptureSignificance: Sheber's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of Judah, connecting him to Caleb, a notable figure. Although he is not directly involved in key biblical events, his inclusion helps preserve the lineage important for understanding the heritage and tribal affiliations of Israel. This genealogical mention underscores God's providence in maintaining the tribes through successive generations.
